definitions.explanation: A hinged control surface on the trailing edge of an airplane wing, used to control the aircraft's roll. Ailerons on the left and right wings move in opposite directions to tilt the plane.

examples.japanese: {副翼|ふくよく}を{操作|そうさ}して{機体|きたい}を{傾|かたむ}ける。
examples.english: Operate the ailerons to tilt the aircraft.

examples.japanese: {左|ひだり}の{副翼|ふくよく}を{上|あ}げると{機体|きたい}は{左|ひだり}に{傾|かたむ}く。
examples.english: When the left aileron is raised, the aircraft tilts to the left.

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}{調査|ちょうさ}の{結果|けっか}、{副翼|ふくよく}の{故障|こしょう}が{墜落|ついらく}の{原因|げんいん}であったことが{判明|はんめい}した。
examples.english: The accident investigation revealed that a malfunction of the ailerons was the cause of the crash.

notes:
A compound of {副|ふく} (secondary/auxiliary) and {翼|よく} (wing). The Japanese term literally means "auxiliary wing," reflecting that ailerons are movable surfaces attached to the main wing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {副翼|ふくよく}を{操作|そうさ}する: operate the ailerons
- {副翼|ふくよく}の{故障|こしょう}: aileron malfunction
- {左右|さゆう}の{副翼|ふくよく}: left and right ailerons

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {主翼|しゅよく}: main wing (the primary wings of an aircraft)
- {尾翼|びよく}: tail wing; empennage (the tail section of an aircraft)
- {方向舵|ほうこうだ}: rudder (controls yaw, the left-right rotation)
- {昇降舵|しょうこうだ}: elevator (controls pitch, the nose up/down rotation)

TECHNICAL NOTE:
Ailerons work in pairs: when one goes up, the other goes down. The wing with the lowered aileron generates more lift and rises, while the wing with the raised aileron generates less lift and drops, causing the aircraft to roll.
